title: UPI Now Works in 10 Countries as NPCI Expands Its Global Acceptance List
excerpt: From Bhutan in 2021 to Cambodia and Greece in 2026, Indian tourists can scan and pay with familiar UPI apps abroad - with in-app activation, Rs 2 lakh European limits, and uneven merchant acceptance to plan around.
body:
• UPI now works for merchant payments in 10 countries — Bhutan, Singapore, UAE, France, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Qatar, Cambodia and Greece — with Cambodia and Greece the newest additions in 2026.
  • NPCI has separately expanded its "UPI Global Acceptance" enablement list, covering more markets including Bahrain, Canada, Kuwait, New Zealand, Oman, South Africa and Switzerland, with European transaction limits raised to ₹2 lakh.
  • Travellers must activate "International UPI" in their app before departure; merchant acceptance abroad is uneven, so an international card and some local cash remain essential backups.

Paying by phone abroad is no longer a novelty for Indian travellers — it is a planning item. UPI, built by the National Payments Corporation of India, now works for merchant payments in 10 countries, and its international arm NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) has expanded the broader "UPI Global Acceptance" enablement list further in 2026. For a generation that reaches for a QR code before a wallet, the map of where that works is worth knowing.

The 10-country list

The bilateral acceptance footprint, consolidated from NPCI's partner table: Bhutan (July 2021, via the Royal Monetary Authority — the first foreign country to adopt UPI), Singapore (merchant payments from August 2021; the landmark UPI–PayNow remittance linkage from February 2023), UAE (April 2022, through Mashreq's NeoPay, Network International and Magnati), France (February 2024, via LYRA Network — the first European country, starting with the Eiffel Tower), Mauritius and Sri Lanka (both February 2024), Nepal (merchant payments March 2024 via FonePay; person-to-person via Nepal Clearing House in June 2026), Qatar (September 2025, Qatar National Bank), Cambodia (June 2026, ACLEDA Bank) and Greece (mid-2026, Eurobank).

Separately, NPCI has revised and expanded the wider enablement list for UPI Global Acceptance to cover additional markets — including Bahrain, Canada, Kuwait, New Zealand, Oman, South Africa and Switzerland, per Mint's May 2026 reporting. The distinction matters: the 10-country list reflects established bilateral partnerships, while the expanded list is enablement coverage that is still rolling out. Pilots have also been reported in Japan and Malaysia, with Cyprus and others in the pipeline — unconfirmed, but indicative of direction.

How to use it abroad

The mechanics are straightforward. Travellers scan local QR codes with their regular UPI apps — PhonePe, Google Pay, BHIM, Paytm — but must first activate "International UPI" in the app: profile, UPI and payment settings, select the account, complete SMS verification, choose a validity window (a week, a month or three months) and set the UPI PIN.

Limits and costs need attention. NPCI set the per-transaction and per-day limit for UPI Global Acceptance in Europe at ₹2 lakh for merchant payments, with banks free to set lower caps. Banks typically apply forex conversion fees of roughly 2–3% on cross-border UPI — similar to international card payments, and a world away from domestic UPI's zero fees. And merchant acceptance is far from universal: in France, for example, UPI works at selected tourist sites, Galeries Lafayette and Paris cafés, not everywhere. Carry an international debit or credit card and some local cash as backup.

UPI's growing international acceptance reflects "trust in India for building technology-led solutions that create value beyond borders and deepen partnerships for shared growth and prosperity."

— Piyush Goyal, Union Minister, quoted in Mint

The diaspora corollary

Beyond tourism, there is a separate NRI utility: NRIs holding NRE or NRO accounts in countries including the US, Canada, UK, UAE, Singapore and Australia can link international mobile numbers and use UPI for transfers to India. Combined with the Singapore PayNow remittance corridor, UPI is quietly becoming diaspora financial infrastructure, not just a domestic payments story.

What's next

The trajectory is clear — from Bhutan in 2021 to a double-digit country count in 2026, with more pilots in the pipeline. The binding constraint now is not partnerships but acceptance density: a QR network is only as useful as the merchants who display it. Until that catches up, the savvy traveller's setup is UPI activated, card in pocket, cash in reserve.
